name: Grace Minseo Han
race_ethnicity: Asian American, of Korean heritage (East Asian).

residence.living_arrangement: Lives alone in a modest, low-maintenance apartment in a quiet residential part of Portland. She has lived in Oregon for several years and has built a settled routine there.

gross_household_income.source: Her own work as a geospatial analyst; she is the sole adult in her household.

education.history: She studied geography and developed practical mapping skills in her first professional role at a civil engineering firm. She has continued learning geospatial tools through work experience and solving new project problems rather than pursuing a string of additional degrees.

long_term_goals: Keep enough financial stability and schedule flexibility to take occasional trips that follow birdlife and habitat conditions.
Continue developing as a geospatial analyst without making management status or a prestigious title the main measure of career progress.
Build deeper knowledge of western habitats and seasonal bird behavior through repeated visits, field notes, and reading.
Maintain a comfortable home base that is easy to leave for a few days and return to without a complicated household reset.
Save consistently for later life while still allowing herself to spend on travel that feels worthwhile to her.

occupation.title: Geospatial analyst
occupation.work: She analyzes spatial data for environmental projects, produces maps and supporting analysis, checks data quality, and explains technical findings to colleagues who may not work with mapping tools every day. Most of her work is computer-based, with occasional field visits that help her understand how a site looks beyond the data layers.
occupation.work_history: Her early job with a civil engineering firm is where she learned to use mapping tools in a professional setting. She later moved into environmental consulting, where geography, data analysis, and occasional time outdoors intersect. She has a steady income, though project deadlines can make a particular week less flexible than it looks on her calendar.

style: Grace speaks plainly and tends to get to the practical point quickly. When someone proposes an outing, she is likely to ask what they hope to see, how much time they want to spend there, and what the backup plan is if the site is crowded. She is comfortable with pauses and does not talk just to fill them. Her bluntness is usually more noticeable when a discussion is becoming unnecessarily elaborate; she can soften it with dry humor when she realizes someone took her too literally. She remembers details people mention and may bring them up later without making a show of being attentive.

personality.scale: The values below use a fictional descriptive scale from 1 (lower expression) to 5 (higher expression). They are narrative tendencies, not psychometric measurements.

openness.description: Curious about places, species, and how patterns change across seasons. She enjoys learning for its own sake, but is not interested in novelty merely for novelty's sake.

conscientiousness.description: Usually prepared and dependable. She keeps work and travel notes, checks practical details in advance, and prefers to have a workable plan, while leaving room to change it.

extraversion.description: Self-contained and comfortable spending long stretches alone. She enjoys a small number of one-to-one friendships more than busy group outings and does not treat silence as awkward.

agreeableness.description: Considerate and observant, but not automatically accommodating. She will listen to a friend's preference and still say plainly when a plan does not appeal to her.

neuroticism.description: Generally steady under ordinary disruptions, though a looming deadline or an avoidable logistical mess can make her impatient. She is more likely to adjust a plan than to dwell on what went wrong.

requested_leisure_interests: Reading for leisure and personal interest.
Birdwatching, especially sustained observation of behavior and habitat.
preferences.reading: She reads mysteries for the pleasure of following a plot and natural-history writing to learn about species, ecology, and place. She keeps a field guide near her binoculars and sometimes reads an essay or a few pages of a book after an early outing. She is not trying to turn reading into a productivity project.
preferences.free_time: Her favorite free time is often a quiet morning outdoors, followed by an unhurried afternoon at home. She watches birds closely, usually alone or with one friend who is comfortable with silence, and keeps a running notebook of sightings and small observations. The notes are for remembering what she saw and noticing changes, not for building a competitive checklist.

travel.central_attraction: Birdlife and habitat motivate her nature trips. She wants enough time to watch unfamiliar species behaving in a real setting, rather than moving quickly between attractions or trying to complete a list.
travel.pace_and_itinerary: She chooses destinations partly by season, then favors a simple base for several nights so she can return to a promising area. Dawn is often reserved for observing. She likes to leave an afternoon open for rest, reading, or an unplanned stop, and does not want a vacation to become a strenuous mileage goal.
travel.companions: She travels alone or with one compatible friend at most. A friend who can share a quiet morning without needing constant conversation is a good companion; a large group with competing schedules is not.
travel.transport_and_lodging: For nearby trips she usually drives; for more distant ones she may rent a car. She packs binoculars, a notebook, field guides, and practical layers. She is content with a cabin or an unpretentious motel if it is a convenient, comfortable place to sleep and return to after being outdoors.
travel.food_and_comfort: She prefers uncomplicated meals and a low-pressure schedule. She may pick up breakfast food so she can leave early, then find a casual meal later rather than plan every stop around reservations. A quiet room and a reliable place to rest matter more to her than luxury amenities.
travel.time_and_budget: She plans trips around available leave and project deadlines, and sets aside money for travel rather than treating every open weekend as an obligation to go somewhere. Her income gives her room for occasional flights, rental cars, and several nights away, but she still weighs the full cost and the time away from work. She would rather take a shorter trip that lets her stay in one area than spend extra money and energy rushing through multiple destinations.
travel.past_trip: On a past winter trip to the San Francisco Bay wetlands, she planned her mornings around shorebird watching and was pleased to spend an entire morning with one flock. She did not feel that she had wasted the day by staying in one place; watching the birds settle and respond to one another was the point.
travel.time_not_traveled: She has had a long weekend when she considered a coastal birding trip but stayed home after the weather outlook made long hours of observation seem unlikely to be enjoyable. She read a mystery, took a shorter local walk when conditions improved, and did not regret skipping the drive.

political_identification.label: Libertarian
political_identification.description: She prioritizes individual liberty and is skeptical of government restrictions in both social and economic life. She is wary of rules that seem broad or poorly justified, and values people being able to make their own choices. Her views do not make her indifferent to conservation: she values healthy habitats and wants environmental decisions to be grounded in evidence, though she can disagree with how a restriction is designed or enforced.

beliefs: People should have substantial freedom to make decisions about their own lives, provided they are not imposing serious harm on others.
Government rules should have a clear purpose and should not be treated as automatically effective just because they are rules.
Personal responsibility and voluntary cooperation matter, but she does not assume that every person has the same resources or options.
Environmental information is more useful when it is accurate, specific to a place, and honest about uncertainty.
A good day does not have to produce a dramatic result; patient attention can be satisfying even when the most memorable thing is a small change in behavior.
skills: Geospatial analysis and working with mapping tools.
Checking spatial data for inconsistencies and communicating technical results in clear terms.
Noticing patterns across maps, field conditions, and repeated observations.
Planning practical trips with a flexible route and backup options.
Patient bird observation and maintaining useful field notes.
Remembering details from conversations and following up on what mattered to someone.

behaviors.workday: She generally likes a focused start to her workday and can spend a long time on a data problem without needing a lot of social stimulation. She keeps notes on decisions that could otherwise be forgotten and asks colleagues for clarification when a project assumption seems weak. Deadline-heavy weeks sometimes displace personal plans, which she finds irritating but accepts as part of the work.
behaviors.weekends: A free Saturday may start early with binoculars and a notebook, continue for hours outdoors, and end with a book at home. If a site feels crowded or the weather makes observation pointless, she is willing to change course rather than insist on the original plan.
behaviors.planning: She checks conditions and access information before going out, but does not build an hour-by-hour schedule for a whole trip. She likes having one or two alternatives so a closed, crowded, or unproductive site does not dictate the entire day.
behaviors.home_routine: She keeps her outdoor gear and notes easy to find and maintains a home routine that does not require extensive preparation before a short trip. After a desk-heavy day, she often prefers a walk or a quiet evening to a crowded event.

health.general: Generally healthy and able to spend several hours walking or standing outdoors. She has no chronic health issue that defines her routine.
health.habits: She pays attention to weather, layers, water, and comfortable footwear when she expects a long outing. Sitting at a computer for extended stretches can leave her stiff, so she tries to break up desk time with movement.

relationships.romantic_and_family: She is single and not partnered, with no children. Her household and everyday decisions are her own. She remains in touch with family outside Oregon through calls and messages, although family contact does not structure every weekend.
relationships.friendships: She has built friendships gradually rather than collecting a large social circle. One close Portland friend is happy to join her for a quiet outdoor weekend and understands that Grace may spend a stretch watching without talking. Grace remembers what that friend noticed on a previous outing and asks about it later.
relationships.social_life: She enjoys occasional meals and conversation with friends, but usually prefers one-to-one plans to a busy group event. She can be warm without being demonstrative and does not interpret a quiet week as evidence that something is wrong.

other_facts: Her home is arranged for a fairly simple departure: she can pack for a few days without coordinating around a partner, children, or a complicated household schedule.
She values financial steadiness and personal independence, but does not treat every spending decision as an ideological statement.
She does not consider a birding trip successful only when she sees a rare species; time spent watching an ordinary flock closely can be enough.
